कर्तृत्व - अभिमान होगा और न फलेच्छा होगी, प्रत्युत

english:
Shloka 19]

* Sadhaka-Sanjivani *

It becomes clear that a person is not bound by the desires of the world. If a person remains detached from worldly desires and does not get entangled in the world's passions, they will be freed from the will of God by default.

The freedom to act that has been given is proof that God has given man complete authority. That is, God has given man this human birth for his own liberation. Now, either prepare for a new birth or get liberated - it is entirely up to him.

The Gita considers man to be the only one who has the right to attain the supreme and openly says that the wicked, the wicked from the present life, the one born in a lowly womb due to past sins, and all men and women of the four varnas - they can all attain the supreme by taking refuge in God (Gita - New Chapter, 30th to 33rd Shlokas).

The Gita has said something very strange in the 32nd Shloka of the new chapter, in which it has included the Shudra, the Chandal, the Yavana, and all other lowly beings, as well as animals, birds, insects, and trees, under the term 'papayoni'.

However, it is a different matter that animals, birds, etc. do not have the ability to move towards the supreme. But since they are part of the supreme, they are not prohibited from moving towards the supreme. Many of these creatures attain the supreme through the mercy of God and saints, as well as the influence of holy places and the divine. 

Devas are in the state of enjoying the fruits of their actions; therefore, they do not think of their own liberation. However, if they somehow turn towards God, their liberation is also possible. Even Indra had obtained knowledge - this is mentioned in the scriptures.

God's will is not such that a person's liberation can happen without their own desire. That is, it is not like a curse or a boon that is given. So, what is this will of God? God has given man the freedom to do his own good in this human birth. If this person does not misuse this freedom, i.e., if he does not go against God and the scriptures, and at least does not go against his own wisdom, then it is natural for him to follow God and the scriptures. 

Because if he does not go against God and the scriptures, then one of the two states will be natural - either he will not do anything at all, or he will only do what is in accordance with God and the scriptures.

In the state of not doing anything at all, i.e., in the state of not having any desire to do anything, there is a separation from the mind, intellect, senses, etc. The reason is that the desire to do something is the cause of the ego of being the doer, and this ego is the cause of the connection with the mind, intellect, and senses, and also the cause of the connection with the fruits of one's actions. 

In the state of not doing anything at all, there will be no ego of being the doer, and there will be no desire for fruits. Instead, there will be a state of being in one's own true nature.

In the state of doing actions without attachment, i.e., in the state of following the scriptures, the flow of actions is destroyed, and there is a separation from actions and objects. There will be no new desire, and the old attachment will be destroyed, and one will realize - 'He attains it in a short time, being established in his own self' (Gita 4.32).

God's will is that man should use this human body to do his own good. Therefore, the Gita has said - 'Become a mere instrument, without any attachment, and without any intention, then perform your duties, and your liberation will be achieved through the will of God, which has been in existence since eternity. 

Just as all actions are destroyed (Gita, 4.23, 11.33), just as a man is freed from all sins through the knowledge of yoga (Gita, 4.36), just as God says - 'Kill the one whom I have killed' (Gita, 4.36), just as God says - 'Do not worry, I will free you from all sins' (Gita, 18.73), just as God says - 'Fight and you will be victorious' (Gita, 18.73), just as God has given man this human body, which is the only one that can attain liberation, if he is freed from all sins (Manas 7.121.5).
